newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes ease with WTI, trade idle.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes ease with WTI, trade idle.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude markets drifted lower Wednesday, with no direction other than Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI) grade to guide local trade, traders said.
No new deals or negotitions were reported by traders, who waited on the sidelines to evaluate their supply needs for next month.
May crude oil futures, the basis for next month's spot shipments, expired late Tuesday, leaving buyers and sellers to negotiate a new price formula temporarily.
Physical deliveries of May WTI crude eased five cents in midday New York trade.
Outright prices stood at $18.13/18.33 a barrel, in line with the fall in WTI..
A trading house was heard offering South Blend cargo (29 API, 0.8 sulphur) to West Coast (PADD 5) refiners at a price rumored to be 60 to 80 cents a gallon under ANS.
The grade does not require as much desulphurization as ANS, according to some buyers, and makes it more economical to process into light products.
Two were sized at 4,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) for May, and a third for 5,000 bpd.
On a notional basis, Line 63 was talked $2.37/2.27 under May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI). The grade rarely trades off WTI.
In heavy crude markets, all California lowered prices for Point Arguella offshore crude by 0.50 cents a barrel as of April 17.
With more Venezuelan and Mexican heavy grades moving into the U.S. Gulf, shipments of Point Arguello east have been discounted into the West Coast, traders said.
